# select_team_role (Resource)

One role granted to a team, on the whole organization or on one resource. Every member of the team holds the role. Use one of these per grant.

## About

Each `select_team_role` grants one role to one team, on one scope. Every member of the team, including the members of an SSO group on the team, holds the role. Grants that Terraform does not manage are not changed.

Omit `scope` to grant the role on the whole organization. To grant it on one resource, set `scope.type` and `scope.id`. A `usage_group` scope accepts only the `viewer` role; the provider rejects any other role on it at plan time.

This resource is backed by SELECT's v2 API, at `/v2/teams/{team_id}/roles`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "select_team" "analysts" {
  name = "Analysts"
}

resource "select_usage_group_set" "departments" {
  name  = "Departments"
  order = 1
}

resource "select_usage_group" "marketing" {
  name               = "Marketing"
  order              = 1
  usage_group_set_id = select_usage_group_set.departments.id

  filter_expression_json = jsonencode({
    operator = "and"
    filters = [
      {
        field    = "role_name"
        operator = "in"
        values   = ["MARKETING"]
      }
    ]
  })
}

# Every member of the team can view the Marketing usage group. A usage_group
# scope accepts only the viewer role.
resource "select_team_role" "analysts_marketing" {
  team_id = select_team.analysts.id
  role    = "viewer"
  scope = {
    type = "usage_group"
    id   = select_usage_group.marketing.id
  }
}

# Without a scope, the role applies to the whole organization.
resource "select_team_role" "analysts_monitors" {
  team_id = select_team.analysts.id
  role    = "monitor_editor"
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `role` (String) The role to grant: `admin`, `editor`, `monitor_editor`, `viewer` or `team_creator`. A `usage_group` scope accepts only `viewer`. Changing it forces a new grant.
- `team_id` (String) The team to grant the role to. Every member of the team holds the role. Changing it forces a new grant.

### Optional

- `scope` (Attributes) The resource the role applies to. Omit it to grant the role on the whole organization. `id` is required for every `type` except `organization`. Changing it forces a new grant. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--scope))

### Read-Only

- `create_time` (String) When the role was granted to the team — RFC 3339 UTC.
- `id` (String) The grant's identifier in SELECT, assigned when the role is granted. Use it with `terraform import`, as `team_id/id`, to bring an existing grant under management.

<a id="nestedatt--scope"></a>
### Nested Schema for `scope`

Required:

- `type` (String) The kind of resource the grant applies to: `organization`, `snowflake_organization`, `snowflake_account`, `databricks_account`, `databricks_connection`, `bigquery_connection`, `aws_account`, `tableau_site` or `usage_group`.

Optional:

- `id` (String) The resource's identifier: the Snowflake organization name, the Snowflake account UUID, the Databricks account id, or the id SELECT gave the Databricks connection, BigQuery connection, AWS account, Tableau site (its LUID) or usage group. Leave it unset for `organization`.

## Import

`select_team_role` can be imported using the team ID and the grant ID, separated by a forward slash:

```bash
terraform import select_team_role.example <team_id>/<role_id>
```

To find the grant ID, list the team's role grants with the API:

```bash
curl -s https://api.select.dev/v2/teams/$TEAM_ID/roles \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SELECT_API_KEY" \
  -H "x-tenant-id: $SELECT_ORGANIZATION_ID" | jq '.items[] | {id, role, entity}'
```

## Additional Information

### Every change replaces the grant

The API cannot change a team role grant. A change to `team_id`, `role` or `scope` revokes the grant and makes a new one.

### How the provider reads a grant

The API has no route that returns one team role grant, so the provider lists the team's grants and finds this one by its ID. If the grant is not in the list, for example because someone revoked it in the SELECT UI, the next plan grants it again.

### A grant that already exists

If SELECT refuses the grant with a conflict, the same role can already be granted to the team on the same scope. Import that grant instead of creating it again.
